thread:
morgan: Quick follow-up from today's RFC review — I'm proposing we explore a proxyless tenant-egress option where identity binding happens at the control plane level instead of a sidecar. Thoughts?

rachel: Curious what you mean by "identity binding at the control plane". Do you mean issuing per-tenant mTLS certs on connect and using those to stamp egress flow identity?

morgan: Exactly. Two pieces: 1) control plane mints short-lived certs tied to tenant id / workload-id; 2) dataplane NAT preserves the source ip but we map cert identity back to tenant for audit and policy. No sidecar changes to app.
jason: Sounds nice for app simplicity, but how do we enforce egress policies without local enforcement point? Would we push policy to the dataplane router/ENI?
priya: We also need to worry about SNAT/IP preservation for customers who expect fixed outbound IPs. If we rely on shared NAT, mapping cert->tenant could break IP-based allowlists.
morgan: Yeah — option A: give each tenant a stable egress IP (reserved ENI per tenant) — expensive at scale. Option B: ephemeral IP pool + control plane exposes an identity header for downstream (proxyless) consumers — but that relies on customer trusting headers.
rachel: For regulated customers we can't depend on header trust. They want cryptographic provenance. So per-tenant certs mTLS to downstreams is the only strong option, but that requires terminations we may not control.
jason: Operational concerns: cert churn, revocation, and tokens. How short-lived are certs? If too short, we risk heavy control plane load issuing certs on scale (thousands TPS).
priya: Also, what happens during failover? If control plane is unavailable, do new flows fail open/closed? We need a fallback semantics that doesn't break customers.
morgan: Proposal sketch:
- Cert TTL = 1h (refreshable by long-lived token)
- Local dataplane caches mapping tenant-id -> current cert thumbprint and enforces policy locally (no sidecar required, router does enforcement)
- For customers needing stable egress IPs, we offer an opt-in reserved-ip bucket (paid)
- Audit: control plane logs cert issuance & dataplane emits tenant mapping in flow logs (signed at rest)

Questions: can nginx/envoy-free apps still present identity to downstreams? For proxyless patterns we'd rely on dataplane to inject signed attestation (like a JWT) to downstreams — but again header trust limits this for regulated workloads.

jason: Implementation risk list: cert issuance QPS, dataplane cache invalidation, rollout path for existing dedicated customers, and egress-cost accounting.
priya: Ops/playbook needed: how to revoke a tenant's certs if compromised, how to rotate, and how to audit who requested certs. Also SLOs for control plane issuance.
morgan: Good notes. Action items I propose:
1) Spike: implement a small proof-of-concept where control plane issues tenant certs and our regional relay (dataplane) validates and maps to tenant-id, injects a signed attestation header. (owner: morgan)
2) Perf test: measure cert issuance QPS and cache hit ratios using synthetic workload (owner: jason)
3) Security review: validate threat model for header attestation vs mTLS end-to-end (owner: priya)
4) Pricing/ops: model reserved-ip cost and make opt-in plan for customers needing fixed egress ips (owner: rachel)

rachel: +1. Also add a canary that restricts this to non-regulated tenants at first — experiment with header attestation for downstreams.
jason: For the spike, I'll mock a small CA in staging and wire up our relay. I'll add a simple cache expiry hook so we can tune TTL.
priya: I'll schedule a short threat-model sync with security next week. We should decide fail-open vs fail-closed before any customer rollout.
infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: staging-spike/tenant-cert-spike -> tomorrow 08:00 UTC. (status: queued) :hammer_and_wrench:
morgan: Thanks all — I'll create the RFC follow-up doc with the sketch above and link the spike PR when ready.

(reacted: rachel :thumbsup:, jason :eyes:)
